title: Conditional probability: restrict, then count again

steps.label: All 100 emails
steps.pseudocode: Start with every email as equally likely to be picked.
steps.python:
counts = {
    (True, True): 24,    # spam, contains 'free'
    (True, False): 16,   # spam, no 'free'
    (False, True): 6,    # not spam, contains 'free'
    (False, False): 54,  # not spam, no 'free'
}
total = sum(counts.values())
print(total)   # 100

steps.label: Event A: the email is spam
steps.pseudocode: P(A) = number of spam emails / all emails.
steps.python:
counts = {
    (True, True): 24,    # spam, contains 'free'
    (True, False): 16,   # spam, no 'free'
    (False, True): 6,    # not spam, contains 'free'
    (False, False): 54,  # not spam, no 'free'
}
total = sum(counts.values())
spam = counts[(True, True)] + counts[(True, False)]
print(spam, spam / total)   # 40 0.4

steps.label: New information: B = contains 'free'
steps.pseudocode: We learn the email has the word 'free'. Count how many emails do.
steps.python:
counts = {
    (True, True): 24,    # spam, contains 'free'
    (True, False): 16,   # spam, no 'free'
    (False, True): 6,    # not spam, contains 'free'
    (False, False): 54,  # not spam, no 'free'
}
total = sum(counts.values())
free = counts[(True, True)] + counts[(False, True)]
print(free)   # 30

steps.label: Restrict attention to B
steps.pseudocode: Throw away every email without 'free'. Only B remains.
steps.python:
counts = {
    (True, True): 24,    # spam, contains 'free'
    (True, False): 16,   # spam, no 'free'
    (False, True): 6,    # not spam, contains 'free'
    (False, False): 54,  # not spam, no 'free'
}
total = sum(counts.values())
free = counts[(True, True)] + counts[(False, True)]
print(free, 'of', total, 'emails remain')   # 30 of 100 emails remain

steps.label: The overlap: spam AND free
steps.pseudocode: Count the emails that are both spam and contain 'free'.
steps.python:
counts = {
    (True, True): 24,    # spam, contains 'free'
    (True, False): 16,   # spam, no 'free'
    (False, True): 6,    # not spam, contains 'free'
    (False, False): 54,  # not spam, no 'free'
}
total = sum(counts.values())
print(counts[(True, True)])   # 24

steps.label: The ratio: overlap / B
steps.pseudocode: P(A | B) = count(A and B) / count(B)
steps.python:
counts = {
    (True, True): 24,    # spam, contains 'free'
    (True, False): 16,   # spam, no 'free'
    (False, True): 6,    # not spam, contains 'free'
    (False, False): 54,  # not spam, no 'free'
}
total = sum(counts.values())
free = counts[(True, True)] + counts[(False, True)]
print(counts[(True, True)] / free)   # 0.8

steps.label: Evidence changes the prediction
steps.pseudocode: The prediction changes once the evidence is known.
steps.python:
counts = {
    (True, True): 24,    # spam, contains 'free'
    (True, False): 16,   # spam, no 'free'
    (False, True): 6,    # not spam, contains 'free'
    (False, False): 54,  # not spam, no 'free'
}
total = sum(counts.values())
spam = counts[(True, True)] + counts[(True, False)]
free = counts[(True, True)] + counts[(False, True)]
print(spam / total, counts[(True, True)] / free)   # 0.4 0.8
